subject: history_social
passage: For centuries, weavers near Dhaka, in present-day Bangladesh, produced muslin so fine that it was prized across Asia and Europe. By the late 1800s, however, the industry had all but disappeared. Many historians attribute its collapse to colonial trade policy: under British rule, cheap machine-made cloth from Lancashire flooded local markets, while heavy duties made Bengali textiles costly to sell in Britain.
passage_b: Competition from factory cloth undoubtedly ruined the muslin trade, but historian Farzana Haque argues that it cannot by itself explain why later attempts to revive the craft have struggled. The finest muslin depended on phuti karpas, a delicate cotton that grew along the Meghna River. Once weavers stopped buying it, farmers ceased to grow it, and the plant was eventually lost, leaving later weavers without the fiber their predecessors had relied on.
stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the explanation in Text 1?

choices.A: By rejecting it on the grounds that factory cloth never competed with muslin
choices.B: By arguing that the loss of a cotton plant, not trade policy, caused the collapse
choices.C: By suggesting that British duties on Bengali cloth were lower than historians assume
choices.D: By accepting it but adding a reason why the craft has proved difficult to revive

explanation.why: Text 1 attributes the collapse of Dhaka's muslin industry to British trade policy and factory cloth. Text 2 agrees that factory competition "undoubtedly ruined the muslin trade" but says this "cannot by itself explain" why revival has struggled: the special cotton the weavers needed was lost. So Text 2 accepts the explanation for the collapse and adds a separate reason the craft is hard to restore.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Text 2 says competition from factory cloth "undoubtedly ruined the muslin trade."
explanation.B: Incorrect. Text 2 uses the loss of phuti karpas to explain why revival has struggled, not why the industry collapsed in the first place.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Text 2 does not discuss the size of British duties.
explanation.D: Correct. Text 2 accepts that factory cloth ruined the trade and adds that the loss of phuti karpas made the craft hard to bring back.
